items.Sentence: The new grease interceptor tank and combined septic/pump tank from the Phase 1 upgrade will remain in place and continue to serve as primary treatment for the restaurant.

The dosing compartment of the 15,000-gallon combination septic/pump tank is equipped with duplex submersible pumps (Goulds Model 3887 BHF No. WS1012BHF) as well as floats for pump controls and high water level alarm.
The combined septic tank effluent from the site will be pumped to the system, through an existing two-millimeter perforated screen.

Effluent from the pre-anoxic chamber of the treatment tank will flow over an existing weir inside the treatment tank into the 13,000-gallon aeration chamber for biological oxygen demand (BOD) removal and nitrification.
The existing 3,000-gallon membrane chamber of the treatment tank will remain as a primary post-aeration settling chamber.
The existing above ground MBR structure will be retained and repurposed. The MBR membranes, pumps, and diffusers will be removed and the MBR tank (treatment tank) will remain in place.
Two new Orenco AdvanTex® AX100 treatment units (AX100 units), designed for blackwater and restaurant waste, will be installed above-ground.
Recirculation will be controlled by two 50 gallon per minute, 0.75 Horsepower pumps.
Disinfection will be provided by a new 280-watt Sanitron® S5000C Ultraviolet (UV) unit.
One sludge tank will be repurposed as an additional settling tank for the secondary-treated effluent from the settling chamber of the treatment tank.

The effluent dispersal system is comprised of a subsurface pressurized pipe network of proprietary manufactured tubing with built-in ‘drip’ emitters (GeoflowTM Subsurface Dripline), installed within the dispersal area.

The subsurface dispersal system will be upgraded during Phase 3. Phase 3 upgrades include replacing the Geoflow subsurface drip tubing and adding soil to the existing dispersal field to increase separation to the seasonally high groundwater table.
